run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: The requested index app-262-prod-logs is present with exactly five documents, and it does contain the US prod cluster: three ERROR lines are tagged cluster=production-us-east-1 (two from checkout-service, one from payment-service) between 2026-11-23T15:29:02Z and 16:59:02Z, while two INFO lines tagged production-eu-west-1 report checkout-service healthy at 16:29:02Z and 16:59:02Z. The US errors form a chain: checkout-service 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)' at 15:29:02Z; payment-service 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 16:29:02Z; checkout-service 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)' at 16:59:02Z — so the deepest dependency named in the evidence is the external payment provider call (stripe-us /v1/charges) exceeding the 30s timeout, and the checkout circuit-breaker reading is a consequence recorded later. Corroboration is missing: every Prometheus and Jaeger call in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so there is no error-rate, latency or span-level evidence for production-us-east-1 and no visibility into stripe-us itself; the analysis rests on five log documents. The Kubernetes cluster I could read is a different cluster — its own alerting rule labels it cluster=opspilot-m1 with deployments named checkout and payment in namespace otel-demo — and it looks healthy at ~17:29Z (all otel-demo pods Running/Ready, restartCount 0, checkout pod logging successful payments up to 17:27:10Z), so it neither clears nor implicates production-us-east-1. Conclusion is partial: the provider-side timeout is the deepest cause the logs support, but whether it was provider slowness, a network path problem or a 30s client deadline, and what changed at ~15:29Z, could not be established.

claims.text: The only index in this Elasticsearch target is app-262-prod-logs (open, green, 5 documents), and its mapping has timestamp (date) plus keyword fields cluster, level, service and a text message field.

Inside the authorized window app-262-prod-logs holds 5 documents with timestamps from 2026-11-23T15:29:02Z to 2026-11-23T16:59:02Z, grouped exactly as: production-eu-west-1|INFO|checkout-service 2, production-us-east-1|ERROR|checkout-service 2, production-us-east-1|ERROR|payment-service 1.
production-us-east-1 checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T15:29:02Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)'.
production-us-east-1 payment-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T16:29:02Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.

production-us-east-1 checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T16:59:02Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)'; the same document is returned alone with this error by the last-hour view of the index.
The only checkout records tagged cluster=production-eu-west-1 are INFO and healthy: 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms' at 2026-11-23T16:29:02Z and 'Healthy: success rate 99.7%' at 2026-11-23T16:59:02Z.

The Kubernetes cluster reachable in this Run identifies itself as cluster opspilot-m1 (label set on its alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh, opspilot_integration_id m0-otel-20260909); it has namespace otel-demo only for the application workloads, with Deployments named 'checkout' and 'payment' rather than the 'checkout-service' and 'payment-service' names in the prod logs, and no namespace or object tied to production-us-east-1 or production-eu-west-1.

On cluster opspilot-m1 at ~2026-11-23T17:29Z every otel-demo pod (including checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm) was phase Running with all containers ready and containerStatuses restartCount 0, and its checkout pod logged 'payment went through' for every PlaceOrder through 2026-11-23T17:27:10Z.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in cluster opspilot-m1 holds demo.flagd.json in which every fault flag is state ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off', including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%', variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable', variants on/off).

A blanket 'checkout is down' reading is not supported: the only checkout-service records for production-eu-west-1 are healthy INFO lines at the same timestamps as the US errors, and the reachable opspilot-m1 checkout pod shows consecutive successful payments with zero restarts.

Fault injection through the flagd payment flags was considered and is not supported for the cluster I could read: in flagd-config both paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are 'off', so they do not explain any failure there. This flag data belongs to cluster opspilot-m1 and says nothing about flag state in production-us-east-1.

The production-us-east-1 checkout incident traces to payment-service's outbound charge call to the external provider stripe-us /v1/charges not completing within 30s, with checkout-service's circuit-breaker opening against payment-service (failure rate 44%) as the downstream consequence recorded at 16:59:02Z. The alternative readings of the same error text — provider-side slowness versus a network/connectivity problem on the payment-service side versus an aggressive 30s client deadline — cannot be separated without provider or network telemetry.

A change in production-us-east-1 at or shortly before 15:29:02Z (deployment, config or provider credential/endpoint change) is an unresolved alternative trigger; it was considered and could not be tested because the change_history integration is not available in this Run and no Kubernetes objects for that cluster are reachable.

Confirm with the Stripe-US provider status/incident feed whether /v1/charges was slow or failing around 2026-11-23T15:29Z-17:00Z, and check payment-service's HTTP client timeout, retry and circuit-breaker settings plus its egress path/DNS resolution to the provider, before treating the 30s timeout as purely provider-side.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable throughout this Run: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names and get_all_labels each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (last attempt 2026-11-23T17:30:09Z), so no error-rate, latency or ERROR-series evidence exists for production-us-east-1; missing series are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable throughout this Run: traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level parent/child confirmation of checkout -> payment -> stripe-us calls and no span status codes were obtainable.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so what changed in production-us-east-1 at or before 2026-11-23T15:29:02Z cannot be checked.

The deep dependency has no telemetry at all: there is no data source for the external provider stripe-us, no provider-side log or metric, and no network/DNS evidence between payment-service and /v1/charges, so whether the provider, the network path or a 30s client deadline caused the timeout is unknown.

No Kubernetes evidence exists for production-us-east-1 or production-eu-west-1: the reachable cluster is opspilot-m1 (label from its Prometheus alerting rules) with only namespaces default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo, so the US prod pods' status, container last-termination reasons, restarts and events were not observable.

Log coverage is thin and asymmetric: the entire index holds 5 documents in 30 days, and no logs at all exist for production-eu-west-1 payment-service or for stripe-us, so service-level scope (e.g. how many requests or users were affected) cannot be sized.

Queries that matched nothing: an all-namespace events read returned zero events (jq result_count 0, status no_data) and a fetch_pod_logs call for pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm with filter 'err|error|fail|timeout|panic' over 2026-11-23T16:29:10Z-17:29:10Z returned no matching lines (190 lines read, 188 removed by the filter, status no_data); both were empty results, not proof of absence.
next_steps: Obtain the Stripe-US provider incident/status record for 2026-11-23T15:29Z-17:00Z to confirm or refute a provider-side charge timeout.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access to quantify checkout-service and payment-service error ratios and the p95/p99 of the payment charge call in production-us-east-1, and to read the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert state at the time.
Review the payment-service HTTP client timeout/retry configuration and its egress/DNS path to stripe-us in production-us-east-1.
Pull the change/deployment record for production-us-east-1 around 2026-11-23T15:29Z (config or credential change to the payment provider) via the change-history integration.

content.alerting_rules:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
